guide.title: Post-Cardiac Arrest (ROSC) Care
guide.lead: ROSC is the start of the next emergency. The heart is stunned and the brain is vulnerable. Re-arrest is common. Get the oxygen, ventilation and BP right, find the STEMI, and take them where they can open the artery.

sections.title: Targets
rows: Systolic 90 mmHg or more; MAP 65 mmHg or more
Rapid cold IV fluids in the field

steps.title: Confirm
steps.text: Pulse and BP. Keep the pads on: re-arrest is common.

steps.title: Airway and breathing
steps.text: Secure the airway; ventilate to the targets; waveform capnography.

steps.title: Circulation
steps.text: Treat hypotension: fluid if the lungs are clear; vasopressor infusion per protocol.

steps.title: 12-lead
steps.text: As soon as possible: STEMI means emergency angiography.

steps.title: Destination
steps.text: PCI-capable cardiac arrest centre where available; pre-notify.

quiz.q: Earliest objective sign of ROSC during CPR?
quiz.explanation: Check for a pulse at the next pause.

quiz.q: Post-ROSC SpO₂ is 100% on a non-rebreather. Best action?
ROSC after VF arrest. 4 mm ST elevation in V1–V4, SBP 82, SpO₂ 96%. Best plan?
options: Treat hypotension (fluid if lungs clear), STEMI alert, transport to the PCI centre
Cold saline and the closest ED
quiz.explanation: STEMI after ROSC needs emergency angiography.

quiz.q: Minimum systolic BP target after ROSC:
Should you start rapid cold IV fluids in the field after ROSC?
quiz.explanation: It caused re-arrest and pulmonary edema in trials; prevent fever instead.

options: Hypo- and hyperglycemia harm the brain and are treatable
It lowers cardiac output and constricts brain vessels
quiz.explanation: Raised chest pressure cuts venous return.

quiz.q: Why keep the pads on after ROSC?
Best destination after ROSC with STEMI?
options: Any hospital without a cath lab

flashcards.question: Definitive sign of ROSC
flashcards.answer: A palpable central pulse with a measurable blood pressure.

flashcards.question: Capnography sign of ROSC
flashcards.answer: A sudden, sustained rise in EtCO₂ (to 35–45 mmHg or more).

flashcards.question: Post-ROSC ventilation
flashcards.answer: 10 breaths/min (1 every 6 seconds), EtCO₂ 35–45 mmHg. Don't hyperventilate.

flashcards.question: Post-ROSC blood pressure
flashcards.answer: Systolic 90 mmHg or more and MAP 65 mmHg or more.

flashcards.question: Why a 12-lead early after ROSC?
flashcards.answer: To find a STEMI: emergency angiography at a PCI-capable centre.

flashcards.question: Temperature after ROSC
flashcards.answer: Prevent fever. Hospitals control temperature (32–37.5 °C); no rapid cold IV fluids in the field.

flashcards.question: Post-ROSC threats
flashcards.answer: Hypotension, hypoxia, hyperoxia, hyperventilation, re-arrest, seizures, abnormal glucose.

critical.scenario: After 8 minutes of CPR the AED says "no shock". You feel a strong carotid pulse; EtCO₂ jumps from 28 to 52 mmHg. She starts to gasp. Your partner moves to the stretcher.
critical.question: Priority immediately after ROSC?

options.t: Recheck pulse, full vital signs including BP, titrate oxygen to SpO₂ 92–98%, prepare a 12-lead
Cold packs to the groin and armpits
options.f: Not before stabilising airway, breathing and BP.
Keep them on in case of re-arrest.

options.t: Ventilate fast to bring the EtCO₂ down

critical.explanation: Confirm, stabilise, 12-lead, then decide the destination.
critical.kpi: Prioritises post-ROSC reassessment and stabilisation over secondary interventions

critical.scenario: ROSC with inferior STEMI. BP 88/52, HR 115, lungs clear, opens eyes to pain. Non-PCI hospital 8 minutes away; PCI centre 22 minutes away.
critical.question: Best destination?

options.t: The PCI centre, treating hypotension with fluid en route
options.f: Correct. He needs the artery opened.

options.t: Stay on scene until the BP is normal

critical.explanation: Keep the pads on and be ready for re-arrest.
critical.kpi: Transport destination decision-making in post-ROSC STEMI

critical.scenario: Intubated after ROSC, a 70-year-old is being bagged at about 22 breaths/min with big breaths. SpO₂ 99%, BP 118/74, EtCO₂ 22 mmHg.
critical.question: Most important ventilation change?

options.t: Slow to 10 breaths/min with gentle breaths, aiming for EtCO₂ 35–45 mmHg

critical.explanation: Over-ventilation raises chest pressure, lowers cardiac output and narrows brain vessels.
critical.kpi: Avoidance of hyperventilation in post-arrest care
